events.title: Emperor Valentinian III murders his general Aetius
events.description: Valentinian III killed Flavius Aetius with his own hands during a meeting in Ravenna. The West lost the commander who had checked Attila; Valentinian was himself assassinated six months later.

events.title: Deposed Edward II dies at Berkeley Castle
events.description: Edward II was announced dead at Berkeley Castle, almost certainly murdered on the orders of Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer. The later tale of a red-hot poker is unsupported.
events.html: Edward II was announced dead at Berkeley Castle, almost certainly murdered on the orders of Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer. The later tale of a red-hot poker is unsupported.

events.title: Jacobites rout a government army at Prestonpans
events.description: Bonnie Prince Charlie's Highlanders routed Sir John Cope's army in a few minutes near Edinburgh. The victory encouraged the Jacobite invasion of England, which turned back at Derby.

events.title: H. G. Wells is born in Bromley
events.description: Herbert George Wells was born in Kent to a shopkeeper's family. His novels The Time Machine and The War of the Worlds helped found modern science fiction.
events.html: Herbert George Wells was born in Kent to a shopkeeper's family. His novels The Time Machine and The War of the Worlds helped found modern science fiction.

events.title: Belize becomes independent
events.description: The former British Honduras became independent as Belize, with George Price as prime minister. British troops remained because Guatemala claimed the territory; it recognised Belize in 1991.

intl.name: International Day of Peace
intl.description: Established by the United Nations in 1981 and observed with a global ceasefire since 2001, the International Day of Peace invites all nations and peoples to commit to peace above all differences and to contribute to building a culture of peace.
